title: An Evaluation of Requirements Modeling for Cyber-Physical Systems via LLMs

model.params_source: paper Sec. IV.D / V.D (greedy sampling, temperature 0); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: all (2,633 requirement sentences = the union of the ten released test folds, each with its own train fold)
task.approximation: None beyond the model alias: folds and retrieved shots are the authors' own released files, the prompt is the release's prompt/ner.txt assembled exactly as src/llm/gpt_inference.py (3 shots, single user turn, temperature 0); max_tokens assumed.

items.source: https://github.com/publicsubmission/CPSBench (public mirror of the CPSBench replication package, pushed 2024-08-03): prompt/ner.txt, data/dataset/10-fold/fold_k/{train,test}_data.json (2,633 sentences, KFold seed 42), input/fold_k/shot.json (SimCSE-retrieved shot ids), src/llm/gpt_inference.py, src/eval.py
items.license: unknown (no LICENSE file in the mirror)

prompt.user_template:
## Task Description
You are an expert specialising in building problem diagrams and entity extraction. 
Given the sentence from a software requirements specification, extract all entities that match the schema definition and return an empty list for non-existent entity types.
Please answer in the format of a JSON string. 

## Schema Definition
['Machine Domain', 'Physical Device', 'Environment Entity', 'Design Domain', 'Requirements', 'Shared Phenomena']
'Machine Domain': is the system or software.
'Physical Device': is a device in the real world, which can be used to get/send/receive data/information. 
'Environment Entity': is an entity in the real world. Here are some examples: the patient, the sun, the old.
'Design Domain': is a manually designed domain that can store data messages. Here are some examples: a database, a magnetic stripe card, a tap, hard disk.
'Requirements': is the aim and purpose of the system to be developed. 
'Shared Phenomena': is a set of shared events, states and values between the connected entities.
{examples}
## Test
Input:{input_req}
Answer:

placeholders.examples:
hook: '
## Examples
' + 'Input:<text>
Answer:<entity dict repr>
' for the first three ids of input/fold_k/shot.json

prompt.few_shot: k=3 retrieved from the training folds by SimCSE cosine similarity (Sec. V.D 'Shot Retrieval')
prompt.source_location: Fig. 4 and the release file prompt/ner.txt; assembly in src/llm/gpt_inference.py (get_ner_prompt)
prompt.verbatim: full (release prompt/ner.txt; the four definitions missing from Fig. 4 come from the same file)

output.parse: json field: the first {...} dict in the completion, keys = entity types, values = lists of entity strings (single-quoted Python-dict style accepted)
output.postprocess: strip and lowercase entity strings, collapse whitespace; unparsable output counted as an empty prediction

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: micro P/R/F1 over entity mentions of all six types with exact string match, TP/FP/FN summed over all sentences (src/eval.py compute_f1 = Eq. 5, 'Entity Ave' column); reported x100
metric.original_location: TABLE III, block 3-shot, row gpt-4, column Entity Ave (P/R/F1 = 43/54/48)

notes: The triage tier is 'low' but 2,633 sentences x 3 seeds is about 7.9k calls with 3-shot prompts. || [hooks_4 2026-09-07] the anonymous.4open.science link is dead but github.com/publicsubmission/CPSBench carries the full package; hook rebuilds the authors' 3-shot prompts from it. gpt_inference.py writes only fold_0 by default; the paper reports 10-fold CV, so all ten test folds are items.
